title: Hydroponic Seedling Culture for Low-Contaminant Wheat Tissue Collection
author: Daniela Miller
materials: Return the tube cap and weigh the sample.

steps.title: Wrap and prepare cover tray
steps.instruction: Wrap the cover tray completely with aluminum foil, cut holes where seedlings will be placed, and fold the foil around the edges.

steps.title: Cut and position foam plugs
steps.instruction: Cut styrofoam tubes into thirds, cut a slit halfway into one side of each slice, and insert each slice into the corresponding foil‑wrapped hole in the cover tray.

steps.title: Prepare 1:1 nutrient solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 dilution of the NCSU Phytotron Nutrient Solution (or another suitable solution) according to the recipe; the solution can be obtained directly from the Phytotron watering hose if using those chambers.

steps.title: Add nutrient solution to tank
steps.instruction: Add 16 L of the prepared 1:1 nutrient solution to the hydroponic tank.

steps.title: Set up aeration system
steps.instruction: Attach tubing to the air pump, place the tubing at the bottom of the water tank, plug in the pump, and run it at a low setting so that the water is evenly oxygenated.

steps.title: Prepare germination boxes
steps.instruction: For each genotype, line a clear plastic germination box with a moistened (not wet) paper towel, place 10–20 seeds evenly on the towel, cover with the clear lid, and position the box near a window to germinate. Replace the moistened paper towel every few days to avoid mold growth.

steps.title: Transplant seedlings into foam plugs
steps.instruction: When seedlings have 3–5 roots and the shoot is exiting the coleoptile, gently transfer each germinated seedling into a 3‑inch foam slice, ensuring the roots extend beyond the bottom of the foam and the shoot points upward.

steps.title: Insert foam plugs into cover tray
steps.instruction: Place each seedling‑filled foam plug into its corresponding hole in the foil‑wrapped cover tray, taking care not to damage roots; plugs should fit snugly.

steps.title: Install cover tray in tank
steps.instruction: Place the cover tray, now filled with seedlings, onto the top of the hydroponic tank. Cover any remaining holes with foil or foam to prevent microbial growth.

steps.title: Add distilled water and mix
steps.instruction: Add 16 L of distilled water to the tank and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Maintain nutrient solution
steps.instruction: Replace the 1:1 nutrient solution in the tank every 3–4 days.

steps.title: Monitor seedling development
steps.instruction: Grow seedlings until they reach the 5‑leaf stage; at this point they are ready for tissue collection.

steps.title: Prepare tissue‑collection workspace
steps.instruction: Set up a clean workspace and gather the half‑filled LN2 cannister (filled approximately halfway with liquid nitrogen following safety precautions), a balance, 80 % ethanol, gloves, sterile 15 mL tubes, and tongs.

steps.title: Collect shoot tissue
steps.instruction: Collect 30–50 mg of shoot tissue from each plant and flash‑freeze it.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the plant with its foam plug, detangle roots, gently shake off excess water, and let the plant drip‑dry on clean paper towels.
Wearing gloves and spraying 80 % ethanol between samples, tear off the main tiller shoot at the stem base, discarding any chlorotic or necrotic tissue.
Tare a labeled 15 mL tube on the balance; weigh 30–50 mg of shoot tissue (add additional youngest leaf tissue if the weight is <30 mg).
Securely cap the tube and, using tongs, fully immerse it in LN2 to flash‑freeze.

steps.title: Collect root tissue
steps.instruction: Collect 30–50 mg of root tissue from the same plant and flash‑freeze it.

substeps.instruction: Tare a new labeled 15 mL tube on the balance.
Wearing gloves and spraying 80 % ethanol between samples, gently remove a small section of healthy root tissue, shake off excess water, and add the tissue to the tube.
If the weight is <30 mg, add additional air‑dry root tissue until 30–50 mg is reached.
Securely cap the tube and flash‑freeze it by fully immersing it in LN2 with tongs.

steps.title: Finalize freezing and storage
steps.instruction: Allow flash‑frozen shoot and root tubes to remain in LN2 for at least 20 minutes, then quickly transfer them with tongs to a –80 °C freezer for long‑term storage, avoiding any thawing during transfer.

steps.title: Repeat tissue collection
steps.instruction: Repeat the shoot and root collection steps for each experimental unit as needed.
